newsitem.title: CHILE: Sao Paulo to improve power firms, then sell them.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo to improve power firms, then sell them.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Sao Paulo will try to improve state electrical companies before privatizing them in order to make them more attractive to potential foreign buyers, an official said.

Although Sao Paulo deputy energy secretary Pedro Roberto Cauvilla gave no specific plan, he said Sao Paulo's government hopes the improvements will prevent a repeat of the problems in Rio de Janeiro's sale in May of state-controlled power distributor Light.
He suggested Sao Paulo would avoid clauses that potential investors don't like, such as those in the much-criticized Light privatization.

Chilean power companies, which have big investments in Argentina and Peru, bowed out of the Light sale at the last minute, objecting that the new owners would not be able to pass on higher electricity costs to consumers, and that only Brazilian citizens could serve on the company's board.
"We believe strongly in the question of market prices...and we are not going to force partners to buy into certain clauses that eventually would be a problem," said Cauvilla.
Sao Paulo's timetable for privatisation of its power sector -- which produces more electricity than Argentina nd Chile combined -- calls for the process to be finished by August next year.

The three major power firms, CESP, CPFL and Electropaulo, will be sold more or less simultaneously, though possibly in pieces, he said. "All three are being dealt with at the same time... The contracting, the sale for all three are going to be done together," he said.
